title: The built-in reward
summary: Build the reward a run without a script uses, one idea at a time, and match the Intermediate preset.

steps.title: Slow into the zone
steps.body:
From level 2 on, arriving means rolling into the zone slowly: under 8 m/s with lights and under 4 m/s once people and traffic arrive. Brains that race there arrive too fast and earn nothing.

Over the last 30 m, pay more for new ground the slower the SUV covers it. `route.remaining` is the distance left. One minus `min(1, car.speed / 8 m/s)` is 1 while the SUV crawls and falls to 0 at 8 m/s.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses route.remaining.

hints: The reward multiplies route.gain by how slow the SUV is, and only applies when route.remaining < 30 m.
Multiply 0.1, route.gain and one minus min(1, car.speed / 8 m/s), and add when route.remaining < 30 m. The solution shows the whole line.

steps.title: Every rule costs a little
steps.body:
Small rules cost a little every tick they are broken: speeding, the wrong side of the road, drifting out of the lane and a wheel over the curb. A stop line overrun, a near miss at a light, costs once.

They are small on purpose. A brain still learning to steer should not be scared off the road by them.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses rules.wrongWay.

hints: One line per rule, each with a small minus number.
Write reward -0.3 when rules.overranStopLine, then -0.005 for rules.speeding, -0.01 for rules.wrongWay, -0.002 for rules.laneDeparture and -0.01 for car.overCurb.

steps.title: People and cars
steps.body:
Hitting a car or a person ends the trip. A cost on top makes brains steer clear sooner, and hitting a person costs the most.

`car.crashed` and `car.hitPedestrian` are each true on the tick it happens.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses car.hitPedestrian.

hints: Two lines: one for a car, one for a person.
Write reward -2 when car.crashed and reward -4 when car.hitPedestrian.

steps.title: Match the preset
steps.body:
The rewards and stops are now the built-in reward. The last part is how the next generation is bred: five species, the best fifth of each species as parents, a child mixes two parents 75% of the time and then mutates, and each species keeps its best brain.

Write those settings in the `each generation` block. The check passes when your script does exactly what the Intermediate preset does.

check.message: Your script should do exactly what the Intermediate preset does.

hints: Four calls: speciate, select, breed and keepChampions.
Write speciate(target: 5), select(top: 20%), breed(crossover: 0.75, mutate: { weights: 0.8, addConnection: 0.05, addNode: 0.03, toggle: 0.01 }) and keepChampions().
